abstract.t: OAuth 2.0 access tokens encode an authorization decision made at issuance time. Sender-constraining mechanisms such as Mutual-TLS certificate binding () and Demonstrating Proof of Possession () extend this model by proving key possession at request time, but neither mechanism re-evaluates the full security context against the conditions present at token issuance, nor provides a normative pathway for graduated least-privilege outcomes when that context has degraded.

This document describes the Authorization Posture Mechanism (APM) problem domain and specifies requirements for a mechanism that assembles a per-request Consistency View, evaluates it against the Issuance Posture, and produces graduated, least-privilege outcomes proportional to posture degradation. This revision (-03) adds Gap D: the absence of a normative threat-response pathway for active cryptographic threat events — including Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) interception signals and post-quantum algorithm-agility triggers — and introduces REQ-11 (Threat-Event Integration) and REQ-12 (Algorithm-Agility Trigger) accordingly.

section.name: Background and Motivation
section.t: Zero Trust Architecture, as defined in NIST SP 800-207 , requires that access to resources be granted on a per-request basis using dynamic policy that includes the observable state of the client identity, the requesting asset, and behavioral or environmental attributes.

The OAuth 2.0 framework issues access tokens that represent an authorization decision frozen at the moment of issuance. Revisions -01 and -02 of this document identified three gaps (A, B, C) in the existing OAuth sender-constraining ecosystem with respect to ZTA per-request evaluation. This revision (-03) identifies a fourth gap (Gap D) specifically concerning active cryptographic threat events that require an immediate, normative APM response pathway distinct from the posture-degradation model of Gaps A-C.

section.name: Step-Up Authentication (RFC 9470)
section.t: RFC 9470 defines the insufficient_user_authentication error code and a WWW-Authenticate challenge mechanism. This mechanism is reactive, addresses authentication strength only, and its outcome is binary.

section.name: Rich Authorization Requests (RFC 9396)
section.t: RFC 9396 defines authorization_details for fine-grained issuance-time grants. The claim is static for the token's lifetime. No mechanism exists for per-request narrowing in response to a runtime posture signal or threat event.

section.name: Continuous Access Evaluation (CAEP)
section.t: OpenID CAEP defines asynchronous push events for compliance change. CAEP does not provide a per-request, in-band posture assertion or a normative threat-event response pathway.

section.name: Attestation-Based Client Authentication
section.t: defines a two-token attestation structure. The Client Attestation JWT may be reused across requests until its exp claim, with no normative mechanism to force fresh attestation on a cryptographic threat event.

section.name: Relationship to This Document
section.t: This document defines the APM problem domain and specifies functional requirements for a mechanism addressing four identified gaps:

li.t: Gap A : No per-request triple consistency verification.
Gap B : No graduated least-privilege outcomes.
Gap C : No method-level downgrade on posture degradation.
Gap D : No normative threat-response pathway for active cryptographic threat events including HNDL interception signals and post-quantum algorithm-agility triggers.

section.name: Gap A: No Per-Request Triple Consistency Verification
section.t: No normative mechanism evaluates the certificate, bound token, and device-posture signal together per-request.

section.name: Gap B: No Graduated Least-Privilege Outcomes
section.t: No normative mechanism responds to posture degradation with anything other than a binary allow/deny decision.

section.name: Gap C: No Method-Level Downgrade on Posture Degradation
section.t: No normative mechanism restricts permitted HTTP methods or operation types for an existing valid token in response to a runtime posture change.

section.name: Gap D: No Normative Threat-Response Pathway for Cryptographic Threat Events
section.t: No existing OAuth mechanism defines a normative pathway by which an active cryptographic threat event — specifically a Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) interception signal detected by a network security monitor, or a post-quantum algorithm-agility trigger indicating that the algorithm family used in a currently bound token's cnf key or certificate is being deprecated — can cause an immediate, synchronous, per-request graduated outcome rather than relying solely on asynchronous revocation or manual re-enrollment.

Gap D differs from Gaps A-C in that it concerns active external threat signals — not device-posture degradation — as the driver of the outcome class. The posture degradation model of Gaps A-C assumes degradation is detectable via device-side posture attributes. Gap D covers the class of threat events that are detected by network-layer or cryptographic-layer monitors external to the device, where the device itself may report a clean posture signal while the session is actively under threat.

section.name: Post-Quantum Relevance
section.t: Shor's algorithm solves the Integer Factorization Problem (IFP) and the Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem (ECDLP) in polynomial quantum time. The Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) threat amplifies urgency: an adversary recording TLS sessions today can retroactively recover session keys once a Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer (CRQC) is available, recovering the access tokens exchanged within those sessions.

Gap D addresses the scenario in which an HNDL interception event is detected during an active token's lifetime — for example, via traffic analysis indicating that a session was bulk-captured by a network adversary — and a normative, synchronous APM response is required. The existing OAuth ecosystem provides no mechanism for such a signal to immediately affect the per-request authorization outcome for active tokens without full revocation of the token.

The APM mechanism is algorithm-agnostic: the certificate component of the Consistency View is compatible with ML-DSA certificates defined in as well as current ECDSA certificates. Gap D's REQ-12 (Algorithm-Agility Trigger) formalizes the requirement that an algorithm-family deprecation event can serve as a threat-event driver for immediate outcome escalation.

section.name: Conventions and Definitions
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

dl.dd: A credential issued by an authorization server to a client per §1.4. All access tokens in APM deployments are assumed to be sender-constrained via or or both.

A threat event indicating that the cryptographic algorithm family used in a token's cnf key or bound certificate has been deprecated or is under active attack. An Algorithm-Agility Trigger is a subclass of Threat Event for the purposes of Gap D and REQ-12.

The triple of (a) the TLS client certificate or DPoP public key presented with a request, (b) the bound access token's claims, and (c) the device-posture signal supplied with the request. Assembled per-request at the RS or PEP. For Gap D processing, the Consistency View is extended to include (d) any active Threat-Event Signal associated with the session or token.
An integrity-protected assertion about the security state of the device from which the request originates.
A result of Consistency View evaluation that is neither unconditional access nor unconditional denial. Graduated outcomes include Permit, Scope Reduction, Method Restriction, and Full Denial.

A threat model in which an adversary records encrypted traffic today with the intent of decrypting it using a future Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer (CRQC). An HNDL Interception Signal is a Threat Event indicating that a session's traffic has likely been bulk-captured by a network adversary.
A representation of the security posture of the client and its device at token issuance, recorded by the AS for per-request comparison.
A Graduated Outcome limiting permitted HTTP methods or operation types.
A component evaluating the Consistency View and applying the graduated outcome per §3.
The condition in which one or more attributes of the current device-posture signal are less secure than the Issuance Posture attributes.
The server hosting protected resources per §1.1.
A Graduated Outcome substituting a narrower effective scope, implemented at the RS/PEP layer without modifying the token.

A signal from a network-layer or cryptographic-layer monitor, external to the device, indicating that an active session or token is under a cryptographic threat that the device-side posture signal does not and cannot reflect. Threat Events include but are not limited to HNDL Interception Signals and Algorithm-Agility Triggers.

An integrity-protected, machine-readable notification of a Threat Event, delivered to the RS or PEP via a Threat-Event Integration channel as defined in REQ-11. The Threat-Event Signal MUST be integrity-protected and MUST identify the token, session, or client to which the threat applies.

section.name: The Static Authorization Problem
section.t: RFC 6749 issues access tokens representing an authorization decision frozen at issuance. NIST SP 800-207 Tenet 6 requires: "All resource authentication and authorization are dynamic and strictly enforced before access is allowed." This requirement cannot be satisfied by a token whose authorization context was frozen at issuance.

section.name: The Single-Dimension Binding Problem
section.t: Both and extend the static token model by adding a sender-constraint dimension but remain single-dimension. They do not evaluate certificate revocation, device compliance, or the per-request triple (certificate, token, device posture) for mutual consistency.

section.name: The Binary Outcome Problem
section.t: The RFC 9470 step-up mechanism provides a single escalation path: re-authenticate or be denied. No graduated model permits reduced-scope operations while requiring step-up for write/delete operations.

section.name: The Asynchronous Signaling Problem
section.t: OpenID CAEP operates asynchronously and carries only binary compliant/not-compliant vocabulary. It does not provide per-request synchronous posture assertions or graduated outcome mapping.

section.name: The Threat-Event Response Gap (Gap D)
section.t: Gaps A-C concern posture degradation detectable from device-side attributes. Gap D concerns a fundamentally different class of threat: active cryptographic threat events detected by external network-layer or cryptographic-layer monitors, where:

ol.li: The device-side posture signal may report clean posture because the device itself is not compromised — the threat is at the network or algorithm level.
Standard Consistency View evaluation against the Issuance Posture would produce a Permit outcome, because posture attributes have not degraded.
Nevertheless, the session or token is under active threat that warrants an immediate graduated outcome — minimally Method Restriction or Full Denial — to limit exposure.

section.t: Examples of Gap D threat events:

ul.li: HNDL Interception Signal: A network traffic analysis system detects that a client session's TLS records have been bulk-captured by a passive adversary. The device is uncompromised; the posture signal is clean. But the access tokens exchanged in that session are at risk of future decryption once a CRQC becomes available.

Algorithm-Agility Trigger: A certificate authority revokes an entire algorithm family (e.g., all ECDSA P-256 certificates) due to a discovered vulnerability. Tokens bound to certificates in that family carry a cnf/x5t#S256 binding whose underlying key security is now in question, but the token itself has not expired and the device posture is clean.

Cryptographic Oracle Event: A side-channel or fault-injection attack capability is publicly disclosed that can recover private key material from a specific hardware security module model used in client certificate issuance. Devices using that HSM model have clean device posture signals but are at elevated risk.

section.t: None of the mechanisms in Gaps A-C, RFC 9470, RFC 9396, or CAEP provides a normative pathway for an external Threat-Event Signal to drive an immediate, per-request APM graduated outcome against an otherwise-valid Consistency View.

section.name: Requirements
section.t: Requirements REQ-1 through REQ-10 are carried forward from draft-vicente-oauth-apm-02 without modification. This revision adds REQ-11 and REQ-12 to address Gap D.

REQ-1: Per-Request Triple Assembly. For each Privileged Request, the enforcing entity SHOULD assemble a Consistency View comprising the client certificate or DPoP key thumbprint, the bound access token claims, and an integrity-protected device-posture signal.
REQ-2: Issuance Posture Recording. At token issuance, the AS SHOULD record the security posture as the Issuance Posture associated with the token.
REQ-3: Consistency Evaluation. The enforcing entity SHOULD evaluate the Consistency View against the Issuance Posture synchronously with request processing.
REQ-4: Graduated Outcome Production. The enforcing entity SHOULD produce graduated outcomes: Permit, Scope Reduction, Method Restriction, or Full Denial.
REQ-5: Method-Level Restriction. Method Restriction SHOULD be a distinct outcome class, expressible in HTTP methods and actions.
REQ-6: Scope Reduction. Scope Reduction MUST be implemented at the RS/PEP layer without modifying the access token.
REQ-7: Deterministic Outcome Mapping. A deployment SHOULD define a deterministic, auditable policy mapping posture degradation dimensions to outcome classes.
REQ-8: Integrity-Protected Posture Signal. The device-posture signal MUST be integrity-protected. The signing authority SHOULD be distinct from the client.
REQ-9: Backward Compatibility with RFC 8705 and RFC 9449. An APM mechanism MUST NOT weaken existing sender-constraining bindings. Unknown APM parameters MUST be ignored by non-APM implementations.
REQ-10: Non-Interference with Token Revocation. A Scope Reduction or Method Restriction outcome MUST NOT be interpreted as a token revocation event per .

REQ-11: Threat-Event Integration. An APM mechanism SHOULD define a Threat-Event Integration channel by which an external network-layer or cryptographic-layer monitor can deliver a Threat-Event Signal to the enforcing entity (RS or PEP). The Threat-Event Signal MUST:

ol.li: Be integrity-protected by a trust anchor independent of the client.
Identify the specific token (jti), session (TLS session identifier), client identifier (sub and cnf), or algorithm family to which the threat applies.
Include a threat event type (e.g., hndl_interception, algorithm_deprecation, cryptographic_oracle) from a registered vocabulary.
Include an iat and exp defining the window during which the Threat-Event Signal is considered active.

section.t: When a Threat-Event Signal is active and applies to a Privileged Request, the enforcing entity SHOULD override the posture-degradation-based outcome class with the threat-event-based outcome class if the threat-event-based class is more restrictive. The Threat-Event Signal outcome MUST NOT be used to relax an outcome that posture degradation has already escalated.
The Threat-Event Integration channel MAY be:

ul.li: An asynchronous push from a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) or network analysis platform to the RS/PEP, populating a local threat-event cache keyed by token jti, session ID, or client cnf thumbprint.
A synchronous per-request lookup by the RS/PEP to a Threat Intelligence Service (TIS) for the current token or session.
A signed extension claim in the APM-Posture JWT delivered by a posture attestation service that also has visibility into threat intelligence feeds.

section.t: REQ-12: Algorithm-Agility Trigger. An APM mechanism SHOULD define an Algorithm-Agility Trigger as a subclass of Threat Event (REQ-11) that fires when:

ol.li: The algorithm family used in the cnf/x5t#S256 certificate binding () or the cnf/jkt DPoP key binding () is deprecated by a competent authority (CA, national standards body, IETF WG consensus), OR
A cryptographic weakness in the specific key type used in the bound certificate or DPoP key is publicly disclosed at a severity level meeting a deployment-defined threshold.

section.t: Upon receiving an Algorithm-Agility Trigger, the enforcing entity SHOULD escalate the outcome class for requests bound to the affected algorithm family to at minimum Method Restriction, and SHOULD issue a response that carries a WWW-Authenticate challenge including an alg_upgrade_required error code (see ) advising the client to re-enroll with a compliant algorithm family.

An Algorithm-Agility Trigger MUST NOT be used to weaken the sender-constraint binding verification step (REQ-9). Verification of the existing cnf binding MUST still succeed before APM processing proceeds, even when an Algorithm-Agility Trigger is active.

section.name: Overview
section.t: The APM mechanism operates at three points in the OAuth request lifecycle: Token Issuance (AS records Issuance Posture); Request Processing (RS/PEP assembles Consistency View including Threat-Event Signal per REQ-11, evaluates, determines outcome); and Outcome Conveyance (RS/PEP returns structured response enabling client recovery).

section.name: Consistency View Assembly
section.t: The Consistency View is assembled per-request at the enforcement boundary. Its components are: the Certificate or DPoP Key Component (existing RFC 8705 / RFC 9449 verification); the Token Claims Component; the Device-Posture Signal Component; and, when REQ-11 is implemented, the Threat-Event Signal Component.
Threat-Event Signal Component (Gap D / REQ-11): The enforcing entity checks its threat-event cache or queries the Threat Intelligence Service for any active Threat-Event Signal applicable to:

ul.li: The token jti of the presented access token;
The TLS session identifier of the current connection;
The cnf key thumbprint or certificate thumbprint; or
The algorithm family of the cnf key or certificate.

section.t: If an active Threat-Event Signal is found, it is included in the Consistency View as an additional degradation dimension with a severity class determined by the Threat Event type (see ).

section.name: Issuance Posture Recording
section.t: At token issuance, the AS records the security posture of the requesting client as the Issuance Posture via Strategy A (token claim apm_posture) or Strategy B (server-side metadata per token jti). The apm_posture claim structure is unchanged from draft-vicente-oauth-apm-02.

section.name: Consistency Evaluation
section.t: Consistency evaluation proceeds in the following order:

ol.li: Sender constraint verification (RFC 8705 / RFC 9449).
Posture signal verification.
Issuance Posture retrieval.
Degradation vector computation (device-posture dimensions).
Threat-Event Signal lookup (Gap D).
Combined outcome class determination: the more restrictive of (a) the posture-degradation-based outcome and (b) the threat-event-based outcome.

section.name: Threat-Event Severity Classes
section.t: Threat Event types map to minimum outcome classes as follows. Deployment policy MAY escalate but MUST NOT reduce below these minimums:

li.t: hndl_interception: Minimum outcome class is Method Restriction (read-only operations only). Full Denial is RECOMMENDED for write and delete operations against high-sensitivity resources.
algorithm_deprecation: Minimum outcome class is Method Restriction. Response MUST include alg_upgrade_required error. See REQ-12.
cryptographic_oracle: Minimum outcome class is Full Denial. The session SHOULD be terminated and the token SHOULD be revoked via .

section.name: Graduated Outcome Application
section.t: The four outcome classes are ordered by increasing restrictiveness: Permit < Scope Reduction < Method Restriction < Full Denial. The combined evaluation in step 6 selects the more restrictive of the posture-degradation-based and threat-event-based outcome classes. Outcome conveyance follows the formats defined in .

section.name: Issuance Posture Claim
section.t: The apm_posture claim structure is unchanged from draft-vicente-oauth-apm-02. Sub-fields: posture_at (REQUIRED NumericDate), posture_hash (OPTIONAL base64url digest), posture_alg (OPTIONAL, REQUIRED if posture_hash present), posture_ref (OPTIONAL URI).

figure.name: JWT Access Token with apm_posture Claim

section.name: Threat-Event Signal Format (REQ-11)
section.t: A Threat-Event Signal is a signed JWT whose payload MUST contain:

dl.dd: (REQUIRED) Issuance time of the Threat-Event Signal.
(REQUIRED) Expiry of the Threat-Event Signal. RS/PEP MUST NOT apply a Threat-Event Signal past its exp.
(REQUIRED) A string identifying the threat event type from the registered vocabulary: hndl_interception, algorithm_deprecation, or cryptographic_oracle. Additional values MAY be registered per .

(REQUIRED) A JSON object identifying what the threat applies to. One or more of: jti (token ID), sub (subject), cnf_jkt (DPoP key thumbprint), cnf_x5t (certificate thumbprint), alg_family (algorithm family string such as EC/P-256 or RSA/2048).

(OPTIONAL) The minimum outcome class the issuer recommends for requests matching this threat scope. Values: scope_reduction, method_restriction, full_denial. If absent, the enforcing entity applies the default minimum for the threat_type per .

figure.name: Threat-Event Signal JWT Payload (Algorithm-Agility Trigger Example)

section.name: Consistency View Request Headers
section.t: The APM-Posture JWT header name and structure are unchanged from draft-vicente-oauth-apm-02. Required claims: iat, jti, sub, ath. Freshness window: 60 seconds RECOMMENDED.

section.name: Scope Reduction Response (unchanged from -02)
section.sourcecode: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="example", error="apm_scope_reduced", error_description="Authorization posture degraded; effective scope reduced", scope="records:read"

section.name: Method Restriction Response (unchanged from -02)
section.sourcecode: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="example", error="apm_method_restricted", error_description="Authorization posture degraded; method not permitted", allowed_methods="GET HEAD OPTIONS"

section.name: Algorithm-Agility Trigger Response (REQ-12, new in -03)
section.sourcecode: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="example", error="alg_upgrade_required", error_description="Token binding uses deprecated algorithm family; re-enroll with compliant algorithm", allowed_methods="GET HEAD OPTIONS"
section.t: Clients receiving alg_upgrade_required MUST NOT retry the denied method without re-enrolling with a certificate or key using a non-deprecated algorithm family. Clients SHOULD surface a user-facing notification indicating that a security upgrade is required.

section.name: Full Denial Response (unchanged from -02)
section.sourcecode: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="example", error="insufficient_authorization_posture", error_description="Authorization posture degraded below minimum threshold"

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Security considerations from draft-vicente-oauth-apm-02 (confused-deputy hazard, posture replay, downgrade-forcing attack, side-channel, introspection interaction, non-weakening of RFC 8705 binding, posture signal trust anchors) apply without modification. The following additional considerations apply to Gap D mechanisms.

section.name: Threat-Event Signal Integrity and Trust
section.t: Threat-Event Signals drive outcome escalation independent of device posture. A forged or replayed Threat-Event Signal can cause denial-of-service by forcing Method Restriction or Full Denial outcomes for legitimate requests. Mitigations:

ol.li: Threat-Event Signals MUST be signed by a trust anchor independent of the client and, ideally, independent of the RS. The signing authority SHOULD be a dedicated Threat Intelligence Service with an independently verifiable certificate chain.
RS/PEP implementations MUST validate exp and MUST reject expired Threat-Event Signals.
RS/PEP implementations SHOULD maintain a seen-jti cache for Threat-Event Signal JWTs to prevent replay within the signal's validity window.
The Threat-Event Integration channel (push or pull) MUST be protected by TLS per .

section.name: Limitations of HNDL Detection
section.t: HNDL interception is, by definition, passive — the adversary captures traffic without actively interfering. Network-layer HNDL detection is probabilistic and relies on traffic analysis heuristics (e.g., anomalous bulk capture signatures, timing analysis). False positives may cause Method Restriction outcomes for legitimate sessions. Deployments implementing REQ-11 MUST document the detection methodology and false-positive rate in their deployment's security policy and communicate the implications to end users.

section.name: Algorithm-Agility Trigger as Denial-of-Service Vector
section.t: A broad Algorithm-Agility Trigger scoped to a widely deployed algorithm family (e.g., all EC/P-256 keys) would cause Method Restriction outcomes for all clients using that algorithm family simultaneously, constituting a deployment-wide denial of write and delete operations. Deployments MUST:

ol.li: Restrict the authority to issue Algorithm-Agility Triggers to a small, well-audited set of trust anchors.
Implement rate limiting on the frequency of Algorithm-Agility Triggers applicable to a given algorithm family.

Define a migration pathway that allows clients to re-enroll with a compliant algorithm without full loss of access, using Scope Reduction rather than Full Denial as an intermediate step where operationally feasible.

section.name: OAuth Extensions Error Registry
section.t: This document requests registration of the following error codes in the OAuth Extensions Error Registry ( §11.4):

li.t: apm_scope_reduced: Used in WWW-Authenticate headers to indicate a Scope Reduction graduated outcome.
apm_method_restricted: Used in WWW-Authenticate headers to indicate a Method Restriction graduated outcome.
insufficient_authorization_posture: Used in WWW-Authenticate headers to indicate a Full Denial graduated outcome due to posture degradation or Threat Event.
alg_upgrade_required: Used in WWW-Authenticate headers to indicate a Method Restriction outcome triggered by an Algorithm-Agility Trigger (REQ-12, Gap D, new in -03).

section.name: APM Threat Event Type Registry (New in -03)
section.t: This document requests creation of the "APM Threat Event Type" registry. Initial values:

li.t: hndl_interception: Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later passive traffic capture event. Minimum outcome: Method Restriction.
algorithm_deprecation: Algorithm family deprecation by competent authority. Minimum outcome: Method Restriction with alg_upgrade_required. See REQ-12.
cryptographic_oracle: Public disclosure of cryptographic attack capability against key type in use. Minimum outcome: Full Denial.

section.t: Future values may be registered by Specification Required process per .

section.name: JSON Web Token Claims Registry
section.t: This document requests registration of the following JWT claims in the JSON Web Token Claims Registry ( §10.1):

li.t: apm_posture: Authorization Posture Mechanism issuance posture claim (unchanged from -02).
threat_type: APM Threat-Event Signal threat type (new in -03).
threat_scope: APM Threat-Event Signal scope object (new in -03).
min_outcome: APM Threat-Event Signal minimum outcome class (new in -03).
